Q1: Indeno[1,2,3-cd]pyrene exhibits known carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and/or reproductive hazards (CMR1), as well as acute and chronic environmental hazards (ENV1). It also shows evidence of endocrine disruption (EDC2). However, there are significant data deficiencies for inhalation (IHL4), oral (ORL4), dermal/eye (SKN4), and organ/systemic (OGN4) hazards, meaning its full risk profile in these areas is unknown.
Q2: This chemical is listed on several key 'lists of concern,' indicating recognized hazards. Notably, it is identified by California's Proposition 65 as causing cancer, birth defects, or reproductive harm, and is included on the TEDX list as a potential endocrine disruptor. The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) also classifies it as Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic to humans, and it is subject to EPA's Drinking Water Standards.
Q3: Indeno[1,2,3-cd]pyrene is relatively well-characterized structurally, with a defined molecular formula (C22H12) and substance class, and is not an ill-defined UVCB substance. With 18,000 scientific literature references, it is extensively studied compared to most chemicals in our dataset. Despite this, its hazard profile is incomplete, as evidenced by data deficiencies (Tier 4) in four out of seven hazard categories, including inhalation, oral, dermal/eye, and organ/systemic hazards.
